title: Titanium mineral resources in heavy-mineral sands in the Atlantic coastal plain of the southeastern United States
citation: Van Gosen, B.S., and Ellefsen, K.J., 2018, Titanium mineral resources in heavy-mineral sands in the Atlantic coastal plain of the southeastern United States: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2018-5045, map scale 1:1,600,000.
notes:
Multi-state report; only South Carolina content recorded. Hilton Head Island drilling results are second-hand (McCauley 1960; Williams 1967) and are for groups of holes, not individual logs. Barrier islands reported by Neiheisel (1958) to have high-grade heavy-mineral sands (Bull, Capers, Isle of Palms, Edisto, Fripp, Dewees Islands; page 34) were not recorded as separate observations. Statements that units crossing into South Carolina near the NC border are mapped as Pliocene (page 26) and the modelled titanium maps (figures 10-16) were not recorded. Table 1 (mineral properties) is general, not South Carolina data.
Pages 36-43: conclusions and references. South Carolina-relevant references recorded; references about other states, minerals industry, and methods skipped. No new South Carolina data on these pages.
